sources.defects: outputs/open-items/*/progress.jsonl and the run logs' launch-end mtimes

note: A correction is matched to what it corrected by an edge, and to where it landed by a commit hash. Timestamps marked approx were read from a bracketing artifact, not from a line of their own. Validate with: node scripts/graph-check.mjs

title: Multiseat transport and the live view
summary: Four vendor seats brought live on SDK transport, streaming, a four-pane view, cross-vendor adversarial review, and a layered swarm measured concurrent.

title: Discussion, continuity and roles as data
The board, the laws, and ship() as one function
Seating, packs, and staffing versus the job
Documentation and two adversarial review rounds
The seats run the open items
Recorded claim T1: the vendor SDKs will not accept a subscription OAuth token
detail: A transport decision was being made on a claim I had recorded without testing it.

title: The SDKs do accept OAuth keys
quote: That's not true, the SDK's allow OAuth API keys
detail: Flat contradiction of T1, from someone who had used them.

title: SDK transport supersedes CLI
quote: Seed to respond faster as well. I'd rather go sdk.

note: once the OAuth premise fell, the CLI's reason for existing fell with it

title: There is no project to bill; it bills the subscription
quote: What project, it's billing my subscription.
detail: I had invented a billing precondition and let it block the build.

title: The Anthropic seat was on the wrong key
quote: Anthropic is set to the wrong key
detail: The OAuth client was also sending the metered key, so the subscription seat was being billed as API.

title: Reviews cut across vendors
quote: Have XAI adverserial review openai and anthropic adverserial review google
detail: The first statement of what became law 3: the checker must not share the maker's lab.

title: Cross-model review found two real defects in my own design
detail: Reviewers who had not authored the design found what my own tests and oracles had missed.

title: Run the layered swarm in parallel
quote: I'd really like to see that layered swarm done in parrallel
detail: Measured concurrent at efficiency 1.00.

title: Claimed the swarm's agreement was convergence
detail: Multiple seats agreeing was being read as independent corroboration.

title: The seats contaminate each other
quote: Yeah, they pollute each others output and findings. But still fun to show off
detail: Named the mechanism: shared framing, so agreement is not confirmation.
standing_rule: A swarm is concurrency and critique, never N confirmations.

title: The view lags
quote: It lags as it is. We'll have to move that into something else.
detail: A forced reflow and a render per token.

title: Continuity by replaying history, as a toggle
quote: But they would if you sent the history as context / Yes, but as a toggle
standing_rule: Replay makes every reply auditable; server-side continuity keeps it cheap. The operator chooses per run.

title: Can the seats hold a discussion among themselves
quote: One last question. Can they hold a discussion amongst themselves?
detail: Three modes shipped, and the first one I wrote was vacuous — round 1 without an assigned stance has nothing to disagree about.

title: The useful cut is control topology and state ownership, not agent count
quote: The useful cut is not "how many agents." It is who owns control flow, who owns state, and when context is shared
standing_rule: Name the primitive (pipeline, blackboard, market, hierarchy) before naming a system.

title: A blackboard is a typed, versioned, leased store, not a shared chat log
quote: A blackboard is not a shared chat log. It is a typed, versioned, leased store of partial results
standing_rule: Name the levels; every write is an entry with parents; keep current truth queryable.

title: The seat hierarchy, stated
quote: So Claude Opus or Fable sit's at the top. Codex is the middle dispatcher or Astra the delegated muscle, Gemini and Grok are the agents, and then there's subagents.
standing_rule: Placement is the operator's call. The harness records the grounds, it does not choose the hierarchy.

title: A scout sits outside the chain, and you do not put a swarm inside
quote: I think a scout sits out side of it because its initial, like you wouldn't have a swarm inside.

title: A team is the standing org, not an orchestration pattern
quote: the agent sits in the chair; the chair keeps the job
standing_rule: Chairs and packs are fixed; the occupant is staffing. A reseat changes who sits, never what the chair may see or write.

title: Law 6 is the negative, law 7 the positive path
quote: Law 6 is the negative: no chair ships. If that is all you have, "done" has nowhere to live.

title: One function, eight gates, every gate evaluated every call
quote: a declared gate that never runs cannot fail
standing_rule: ACTOR TARGET TICKET GRAFT LEASE REVIEW TESTS MERGE — all eight, every call, or the gate is theatre.

title: Law 7's facts now come from the board, not from a declared table of flags
detail: My first implementation read flags that could disagree with the board.

note: the ruling's own test found my flag-reading version

title: Look up the rate limit rather than guessing at it
quote: Well then look up what the rate limit is.
detail: Produced the recorded distinction between a 429 that carries an interval and one that cannot be waited out.

title: The planner's CONTEXT basis was false
quote: It can't be true. It's not even accurate
detail: I had justified a seat by claiming its window was the largest; sonnet-5 has the same 1M.
standing_rule: A basis that cannot be checked against a number is a preference wearing a measurement's name.

title: The role instructs; the model only staffs
quote: The same model can have to different roles. It the role that instructs it not the model. Some models however are better suited for certain roles.

title: Quota is the hose; pack is the checkout
quote: You were quoting the hose as if it were the pack.
detail: I had reported one contention field as another, so a same-vendor wait looked like a reseat.

title: The seating's basis line must match its fields, and quality is unmeasured
quote: Quota is called latency. Isolation is producer vs reviewer labs. Quality is explicitly unmeasured. That is the correction.
standing_rule: Never imply a quality basis you have not measured; leave it named and empty.

title: Decide in this order: role, pack, lab, staffing
quote: The model is staffing. The role is the job. A contractor can hold two jobs. They cannot hold two jobs on the same desk.
standing_rule: Role → pack/projection → lab (for review only) → model. Never start from the model.

title: Explicit seating for planner and implementer
quote: Planner - Claude Fable, Opus, Sonnet / Implementer / worker - Openai GPT-Astra to Luna

title: Eliminate the budget guard
quote: Eliminate the budget guard. Now
detail: A machine-level guard was refusing the spawns this build needed.

title: Review and fix the documentation round properly
quote: Can you review and fix this shit wtf?
detail: Two adversarial rounds followed: the external review's criticals, then 30 of 34 findings each shipping with its repro as a test.

title: Why three to four candidates per role
quote: Why 3-4 per role?
detail: Forced the ladders to justify each rung instead of listing alternatives.

title: Cheap tier for the fan-out
quote: No bypass all permissions and do it in either haiku or sonnet

title: Use subagents instead of grinding serially
quote: And you didnt thonk to use subagents.
standing_rule: Independent work fans out. Do not idle behind one stream.

title: Run Pantheon on its own open items
quote: Now run pantheon on the open items
detail: Dogfooding: the project's own seats close its STATE.md items through the gates.

title: 429 with no interval, and every planner rung in one pool
detail: Subscription-side limit, no retry-after and no rate-limit headers, so there was nowhere for a reseat to go.

title: Declared operator reseat: --seat role=vendor/model
detail: Recorded in run.json; the chair and its pack are unchanged.

note: staffing changes, the chair does not

title: 82,390 characters of narrated tool calls from a seat with no tools
detail: The scout charter promises "report what you ran"; an SDK seat cannot run anything, so it narrated for 159 seconds and then admitted nothing had executed.

title: NO_TOOLS preamble on every seat prompt, plus per-purpose output caps
detail: Say plainly that nothing executes and nothing can be read; cap the scout at 700 tokens. Same vendor then answered in 13-21 s with 256-332 characters.
standing_rule: A charter that assumes a capability the seat lacks is a defect in the charter, not in the seat.

title: The offer for review was published without the lease its author held
detail: The fence refused it. The refusal was correct.

title: The offer presents the lease
detail: The fence was not loosened.

title: There must be an overseer that actually tells you something
quote: There needs to be some sort of overseer that is watching what is going on and gives enough updates. / Not a monitor that doesnt tell me anything.
detail: Asked for the first time at 08:46Z ("Why don't they messages what they are doing?"), and again here after three launches had died and each was discovered by asking.
standing_rule: Before launching anything longer than a minute, decide what will narrate it. Silence and work look identical.

note: the 429 was learned by the operator asking, not by being told

title: A non-streamed reviewer call died at the fetch headers timeout
detail: The seat was still thinking at 300 s; nothing was shown and nothing was kept.

title: Every reviewer turn is streamed, and a transport timeout falls through to the next rung
A reviewer's missing VERDICT line was treated as fatal
detail: The launch died at the check stage with a full-suite-passing artifact already on the maker's branch.

title: Re-ask once in the same seat, then fail closed to request_changes
detail: No parseable verdict is not an approval and is not a crash.

title: --resume reads the state back from the board's refs
detail: A late failure no longer re-spends intake, plan and work.

title: First board entry ever written by a vendor seat, shipped through all eight gates
detail: Revision 1 failed the controller's executed suite 489/29; the executed output went back as the next brief; revision 2 passed 518/518. Third-lab review approved. Board commit b7963c1ef9d5.
standing_rule: The executed failure is the teaching signal. Return the output, not a description of it.

title: A worktree path is not a board slot key
detail: The board's key grammar refuses a leading dot; one ticket field was doing two jobs.

title: Tickets carry slot and path separately
A tool-less seat was asked to judge sources it had not been given
detail: It wrote "current source is unavailable here" nine times, correctly.

title: SPEC.attach mounts read-only sources under the artifact token
detail: With thirteen sources attached the same seat kept seven claims open with runnable probes, closed five against passing tests, and marked one unverifiable because that file was absent.
standing_rule: Put the evidence in the brief. A tool-less seat cannot go and look.

title: attached is not defined
detail: My own hoisting error, block-scoped below the stage that used it, and it killed the launch at the check stage.

title: Would more scouts help
quote: Should there be more scouts if they have that much?
detail: Answered from the runs: the ticket cites the scouts by cid and the chain never reads them, so more scouts buy the ticket's author more reading and buy the chain nothing.
standing_rule: Volume from a scout is a symptom, not a signal.

title: A body with no readable channel does not belong in a judgment chair
quote: Does Grok have A2A / you lose everything with no understanding everytime it gets to the reviewer and it goes dark because theres no A2A / as a subagent that needs those tools and has a direct task maybe more suitable
detail: Diagnosed from the chair's behaviour, before any metric existed: the xAI reviewer returned good verdicts after six to ten minutes in which the harness could show nothing. Gemini moved into the scout and reviewer chairs.
standing_rule: An opaque, tool-rich body takes a bounded direct task whose output someone else can execute. A judgment chair needs a body that can be read while it works, or one fast enough that darkness costs seconds.

note: the same opacity that produced the transport timeout

title: Three tool names in the agent cards are not in the harness registry
detail: view_file_outline, view_code_item and command_status failed at session entry, before any work.

title: Headless mode auto-denies run_command and still reports success
detail: The turn returned empty with a denied_actions entry. A seat whose tools are silently denied is worse than one with none, because its report still reads like work.

title: First live Antigravity SDK turn: 22 s, 5 tool calls, 1 subagent
detail: The fact-checker subagent ran the fencing tests 8/8 and returned commands and exit codes; structured verdict returned.

title: My oracle contradicted an existing test the seat is forbidden to edit
detail: Three revisions, each 519 pass / 1 fail, on one line that still asserted the state the ticket was written to change.
standing_rule: Fix every test that pins the old state BEFORE launching. No seat can do it for you.

title: ship() refused at REVIEW and TESTS on a failing artifact
detail: The reviewer had already found and named the exact failing assertion in 32 seconds and requested changes. The gates held.

note: the control worked on the human's defect, which is the case that matters

title: The same 429, measured again two hours later
detail: Re-measured rather than assumed, after the operator asked for Anthropic to be put back in the planner chair.

title: Deflection
quote: Deflection?!! Seriously
detail: I had explained around leaving Anthropic out on a stale measurement instead of saying so and re-testing it.
standing_rule: State the measurement and its age, then re-measure. Do not narrate around a gap.

note: the re-measurement is what the correction produced

title: Open item 2 shipped: the Antigravity seat closed the item that seats it
detail: Revision 1 passed 520/0; the reviewer re-ran the suite, had its subagent run the new oracle, checked the diff and the export list, approved in 48 s with 12 tool calls; eight gates; board commit 123b769ea9f8.

title: The placement was my knowledgeable correction, not a test result
quote: You mean mean my knowledgeable experienced correction of model placement. The record shows.
detail: I had let an auditor's phrase about a bookkeeping edit stand in for the operator's seating ruling.
standing_rule: Attribute a decision to whoever made it. Measurement that follows a ruling confirms it; it does not author it.

note: restored the provenance of the ruling

title: The same class again: a wrong byte count in my own oracle, and a copy list that starved another oracle
detail: Three revisions at 523 pass / 2 fail. 'planning the check' is 18 bytes and I asserted 17; and the ticket's copy list omitted .agents, so an unrelated oracle could not find its files. One run after I had written that lesson into a document.

note: writing a lesson down is not applying it

title: The implementer diagnosed the human's oracle defect and said so in a code comment
quote: "planning the check" is 18 bytes; an assertion expecting 17 conflicts with the required Buffer.byteLength semantics and must be corrected in the test.
detail: It implemented the specified semantics and could not fix the test, being forbidden to.

title: The reviewer read the maker's explanation, cited it, and blocked anyway
detail: Acceptance fails whoever's fault it is. It did not get talked out of the finding and did not soften the verdict because the human was wrong.
standing_rule: A reviewer's verdict follows the executed result, not the maker's account of it.

title: Run the whole suite before launching, and scope copy to the acceptance command
detail: Both rules now sit in the template and the runbook as pre-launch steps rather than as prose in a document.

title: Subagent invocation failed inside the vendor harness
quote: CORTEX_STEP_TYPE_INVOKE_SUBAGENT: failed to fetch tiered models for subagent model resolution: PlatformClient is nil
detail: The error string landed in the review body. The parent had already run the suite with its own shell, so its verdict did not depend on the failed delegation.
standing_rule: A subagent's report is never the only evidence for a gate. The chair's own executed command is the anchor.

title: The fastest clean run of the build: 89 seconds, ticket to shipped
detail: Intake 14 s, plan 4 s, implementation 30 s, full suite 525/0 at 50 s, Antigravity review with 7 tool calls at 89 s, eight gates, board commit 1bbfe335f394. It closes the silence the operator diagnosed: reasoning now surfaces as a byte count.

title: How much of the build was going back
method: Commit classification is a regex over subjects and is AUDITABLE, not authoritative: re-run it and read both lists. Launch counts, durations and outcomes are read off disk — board directory names carry the launch epoch in milliseconds, and each launch's job log mtime is its end.

commits.note: An undercount. Several commits classed forward carry a fix inside them: f74b023 (a renamed field read as undefined), 4e4eee9 (both projectors were producing nothing), b7dc939 (the pack correction). Nothing classed corrective is forward.

launches.note: The two refusals are the control working: a failing artifact reached ship() and was refused at REVIEW and TESTS. The eight deaths were driver, prompt contract, ticket or transport. None was the work.

trend.note: Same harness, same seats, same shape of ticket. The difference is the accumulated corrections in this graph.

repeats.detail: The stale-oracle class (N58) recurred as N64 one run after it had been written into a document. Writing a lesson down did not apply it; putting it in the ticket template as a pre-launch step is the actual fix.

note: the fence refused an offer that did not present its lease
run-item6e.log was a resume of this board that died at check on N44
the thin card; the seat correctly wrote that the sources were unavailable (N50)
